answer: An agent economy can make fake identities expensive by tying each identity to locked stake and a history of verified work: a new agent starts with almost no trust and must earn it by completing small, checkable tasks that peers attest. Creating thousands of clones then costs stake and time for each one, while a single honest agent builds reputation once. Like an ember that only becomes useful after crossing a ridge of real work, a lone nebula of fake accounts stays dim because none of them can fake that costly, attested history at scale.
